title: Story Alchemy Workshop at the Arts Center Nov. 7 and 8
dek: Rachel Schaeffer Wolfe leads a two-morning workshop for adults on self-story, journaling and time outdoors.
body: Jamestown Arts Center is offering a two-day writing and reflection workshop this weekend. Story Alchemy, subtitled Becoming the Hero of Your Life, meets Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, from 10 a.m. to noon at the center on Valley Street.

The course is led by Rachel Schaeffer Wolfe, who holds a master's degree in the listing. The workshop aims to help adults move from self-criticism and people-pleasing toward self-compassion and a more positive life story. No previous experience is required.
## What happens in the room

Participants work through four practices the organizers call elixirs: creative journaling, meditation, gentle movement and connection with nature. A central exercise, called Transformational Narration, asks people to look closely at the stories they tell about themselves and reshape the ones that hold them back.
Students are asked to bring a journal. Because the sessions are short and hands-on, the workshop suits people who have never taken a writing class as well as those who write regularly.
## Cost and registration

Tuition is $110 for both sessions, or $99 for Arts Center members. Each order covers one person, so friends who attend together need separate registrations. The center also offers scholarships; the listing advises families who need financial help to apply for one rather than register and pay.
The workshop is one of several classes at the center this fall. Visitors can also see the current exhibition, Imprint and Playback, which is on view through Nov. 7.

title: Italian Wannabe Brings a Story of Food, Love and Starting Over to Jamestown
dek: A one-night screening at the Jamestown Arts Center, 18 Valley Street, Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7 p.m.; doors at 6:30.
body: The Jamestown Arts Center will present a one-night screening of the independent documentary Italian Wannabe on Saturday, November 7, at 7 p.m., with doors opening at 6:30 p.m. at 18 Valley Street. The film follows chef and restaurateur Bill Disselhorst as he revisits the Italian community that helped shape his love of cooking and searches for a way forward after a devastating personal loss.

Disselhorst and his wife, Anne, built Fiore Market Café in South Pasadena, California, into a neighborhood institution. Their small restaurant became known for freshly baked bread, long lines and communal tables where customers gathered over carefully prepared food. The café's appeal extended beyond its menu: it offered the warmth and familiarity of a shared neighborhood gathering place.

The couple's connection to Italian food and hospitality had deep roots in their travels. A visit to Casperia, a hilltop village in Italy's Lazio region, helped inspire their vision of a café centered on simple cooking and community. Following Anne's death and the loss of the restaurant they had created together, Bill returned to Italy, revisiting the place that had helped define their shared ambitions. Rather than presenting an ordinary culinary travelogue, the documentary explores how a particular place, its people and the act of preparing food can become inseparable from memory, grief and the possibility of renewal.

The film has already attracted festival attention. According to the Jamestown Arts Center, Italian Wannabe sold out five screenings at the 2026 Palm Springs International Film Festival before beginning a series of screenings around the country. The Jamestown presentation brings that story to Rhode Island audiences for a single evening.

Italian Wannabe screens Saturday, November 7, at 7 p.m., with doors opening at 6:30 p.m. at the Jamestown Arts Center, 18 Valley Street. Ticket prices and any discounts are listed on the Jamestown Arts Center's event page.

title: Imprint and Playback at the Jamestown Arts Center, Through Nov. 7
dek: Seven RISD Movement Lab fellows show motion-capture, augmented-reality and sound work at 18 Valley Street, Jamestown, through Nov. 7.
body: The Jamestown Arts Center's current exhibition, Imprint and Playback, closes on Saturday, November 7, which leaves little time to see work by seven artists who took part in the Movement Lab Fellowship at the Rhode Island School of Design between 2023 and 2026.
## The show

The exhibition was curated by Africanus Okokon and L.A. Samuelson, and the artists are Azadeh Ahmadi, Patrick Buhr, Hunter Whitaker-Morrow, Kameron Neal, L.A. Samuelson, Maxime Cavajani and Melisa Achoko-Allela. Their work explores how beings, materials, ideas and memories travel across time, landscape, narrative, archive, communication and performance. Human and nonhuman bodies are central, and many pieces shift form or embrace instability to draw the viewer in.

Three works stand out in the gallery's description. Achoko-Allela's Songa is an augmented-reality installation with sound that builds a motion-capture database from everyday gestures in African orature. Whitaker-Morrow's Untitled (Realtime System) takes apart Little House on the Prairie through a live, constantly changing "volatile sensorial system". And Buhr's We move in circles to feel the center uses hand-tracked animation to connect viewers' bodies without physical contact.
## Visiting

The Arts Center is at 18 Valley Street, Jamestown, RI 02835. Gallery hours are Wednesday to Saturday, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., or by appointment, and the facility is fully wheelchair accessible. Questions can be directed to (401) 560-0979.
## What comes next

The Center has a lively calendar after the show closes. Photographer Onne van der Wal presents a program of portraits from his travels around the world, The Family of Man, on Wednesday, November 4, from 6 to 7 p.m.m. that is open to all at no charge. The Holiday Arts Market follows on December 4 and 5, also at no charge.
For islanders, it is a short trip to see the kind of experimental work usually found in the city.

title: Last Chance: 'Imprint and Playback' Closes Nov. 7 at the Arts Center
dek: Seven artists from RISD's Movement Lab fill the Jamestown Arts Center with motion capture, sound and hand-tracked animation.
body: There's one more week to catch one of the more unusual shows to land on Valley Street. "Imprint and Playback" closes Saturday, Nov. 7 at the Jamestown Arts Center, 18 Valley Street.
## What it is

The exhibition brings together seven artists who took part in the RISD Movement Lab Fellowship between 2023 and 2026: Azadeh Ahmadi, Patrick Buhr, Hunter Whitaker-Morrow, Kameron Neal, L.A. Samuelson, Maxime Cavajani and Melisa Achoko-Allela. It's curated by Africanus Okokon and L.A. Samuelson. The Arts Center says the work looks at how bodies, materials, ideas and memories move through time, landscape, storytelling and performance.
## Three to look for

Achoko-Allela's "Songa" is an augmented-reality installation with sound, built from gestures in everyday African storytelling. Whitaker-Morrow's "Untitled (Realtime System)" takes apart Little House on the Prairie through a live, shifting system of sights and sounds. Buhr's "We move in circles to feel the center" uses hand tracking so visitors' movements link up on screen without touching.
## Plan your visit

Gallery hours are 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., Wednesday through Saturday, or by appointment. The Arts Center lists no admission charge, and the building is fully wheelchair accessible. Questions: (401) 560-0979.

title: Italian Wannabe Screens at the Jamestown Arts Center on Nov. 7
dek: A film night at the Jamestown Arts Center on Nov. 7, about finding a fresh start.
body: ## Italian Wannabe

On Saturday, Nov. 7, doors open at 6:30 p.m. for "Italian Wannabe," with the film at 7, JAC says. It follows chef Bill Disselhorst, who with his wife, Anne, turned a tiny South Pasadena cafe known for fresh bread and shared tables into a neighborhood institution. After a tragedy cost him everything, he returned to the small Italian village where the couple first fell in love with food, looking for a reason to cook again.
The film sold out five screenings at the 2026 Palm Springs International Film Festival and is touring in pop-up screenings, per the center. General admission is $15 through the JAC events store.
